description: Machine-readable ground truth for the DNP3 teaching capture. A control-center master (IP 10.20.0.5, DNP3 data-link address 100) polls and controls a substation outstation (IP 10.20.0.20, DNP3 address 10). After a routine poll/response session and a supervised breaker close, a rogue host at 10.20.0.66 opens its own TCP session and issues control + restart commands while forging the master's DNP3 link address (100). Frame counts and CRCs are asserted by build/verify_all.py.

malicious_frame_detail.meaning: Rogue DIRECT_OPERATE (CROB) trips the breaker with no preceding SELECT and no authentication; outstation accepts it because it trusts the 16-bit link address.
Rogue COLD_RESTART reboots the outstation, denying operators visibility of the site during recovery.

forged_link.true_owner: control-center master at IP 10.20.0.5 (legitimate DNP3 address 100)
forged_link.detection_invariant: A single DNP3 link source address (100) is sourced from more than one IP: the real master (10.20.0.5) and the rogue host (10.20.0.66). Alert when dnp3.src is observed from an unexpected ip.src on control frames.
forged_link.why_undetectable_in_protocol: Base DNP3 (IEEE 1815-2012 without SAv5) provides no cryptographic proof of identity; the outstation cannot distinguish a forged link address from the genuine master.

techniques.name: Unauthorized Command Message
techniques.note: Rogue DIRECT_OPERATE (func 0x05) issues a breaker trip with no authentication or SELECT step.

techniques.name: Denial of Service
techniques.note: COLD_RESTART (func 0x0D) reboots the outstation, denying operator visibility.

ttp.mechanism: DNP3 data-link source-address spoofing (impersonating the master toward the outstation).
cwe: CWE-306 Missing Authentication for Critical Function
CWE-319 Cleartext Transmission of Sensitive Information
ttp.auth_classification: Authentication failure (spoofed identity accepted), leading to an unauthorized control action.

benign_frames_summary.description: Frames 4/6 and 8/10 are legitimate READ polls (func 1) and RESPONSEs (func 129) from master to outstation. Frames 12/14 are an UNSOLICITED_RESPONSE (func 130) event report and the master's CONFIRM (func 0). Frames 16/18 and 20/22 are a supervised breaker close: SELECT (func 3) then OPERATE (func 4), each with a RESPONSE. Frames 29 and 33 are the outstation's RESPONSEs to the rogue host — benign-origin device replies induced by the attacker (not attacks themselves).
benign_frames_summary.note: Non-DNP3 frames are TCP handshake/ACK packets. Only the 14 frames with a DNP3 application layer (start bytes 0x05 0x64) carry protocol semantics.
